title: Japanese Apple Katsu Sauce
description: Grated apple, dates, tomato and a trace of clove make a smooth, fruity brown sauce for spooning over tender cutlets.
equipment: Vitamix or immersion blender with tall heatproof jug

ingredients.name: small sweet apple
ingredients.note: Peeled and cored weight, finely grated.

ingredients.name: coconut aminos
ingredients.note: Use Coconut Secret Original at 90 mg sodium per teaspoon. Low-sodium batch: use 1 tsp total.

steps.title: Stew the fruit
steps.text: Cook {app}, {da} and {w} covered over medium-low heat for 7–9 minutes until the apple mashes easily.

steps.title: Layer the spices
steps.text: Add {tp}, {a}, {cv}, {ms}, {cl} and {al}. Simmer for 6 minutes, stirring often.

steps.title: Blend the katsu sauce
steps.text: Take off the heat and blend until silky. Run a spoon through the sauce and check that the fruit leaves no hard flecks.

steps.title: Check the yield
steps.text: Measure the sauce in a heatproof cup. Aim for 1 cup. If short, loosen with a little hot sodium-free water. If over, return it to the pan and simmer briefly to the mark.

steps.title: Serve the sauce
steps.text: Serve warm or at room temperature with tender pork or chicken cutlets. This sauce also works over cooked cabbage.

notes: Yield: 1 cup, or four 1/4-cup portions. Low-sodium option for the full batch: Use 1 tsp coconut aminos in place of 4 tsp. Use the same final 1-cup yield and 1/4-cup serving. Make ahead: Make the sauce the day before and portion it before chilling. Refrigerate in shallow covered portions within 2 hours and use within 3 days. Freezer-Friendly Verdict: Yes. Freeze flat in 1/4-cup portions for up to 2 months. Whisk again after thawing to restore the texture. Fridge reheat: Reheat a portion in a small pan, stirring to a brief boil and at least 165°F. Loosen with a splash of water if it tightens. Freezer reheat: Thaw overnight in the refrigerator, then use the fridge reheat method. Option A uses the listed seasonings. For a gentler Option B, use 1 teaspoon vinegar and replace half the tomato with additional grated apple. Estimated nutrition per serving (1/4 of recipe): 38 kcal, 0.5 g protein, 9.7 g total carbohydrate, 0.1 g fat, 1.0 g fiber, 96 mg sodium. Low-sodium version per 1/4 cup: 35 kcal, 0.5 g protein, 8.7 g total carbohydrate, 0.1 g fat, 1.0 g fiber, 29 mg sodium. Figures cover the sauce alone. Sodium varies with brands.
